hypothesis: Blind cave species in America are phylogenetically nearer to surface species of America than to European cave species, and likewise for Europe.
pass_criterion: In a time-calibrated phylogeny of cave taxa with surface relatives, at least 80% of troglobitic lineages have their nearest surface relative on the same continent, and fewer than 20% cluster with cave lineages from the other continent.
fail_criterion: Fewer than 60% of troglobitic lineages have their nearest relative on the same continent, or cave lineages cluster across continents more than expected by chance (permutation p<0.05).
interpretation: Darwin's 'affinities' means phylogenetic nearest relatives; 'blind cave animals' means troglobites. No single public dataset with cave-status plus phylogeny was found and fetched.
no_dataset_reason: I did not find and fetch a single public dataset that combines troglobite status, continent and phylogenetic placement. Naming one would risk a fabricated identifier.
